newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal 1997 budget not to boost tax burden.
newsitem.headline: Portugal 1997 budget not to boost tax burden.

text.p: Portugal's 1997 budget will not increase the overall weight of tax although there will be some shifting of the burden inside the various tax bands, Secretary of State for the Budget Manuela Arcanjo said.
Speaking in a weekend television debate, Arcanjo reaffirmed that the government was basing its budget plans on expected economic growth in 1996 of 2.75-3.25 percent.
Inflation was being calculated at 2.25-2.50 percent, while the public sector deficit was targetted at 2.9 percent.
Private consumption is seen rising 2.0-2.25 percent, while public sector consumption was seen rising under two percent.
Exports were seen gaining 9.0-10 percent, with imports increasing 8.0-9.0 percent. Economic growth should boost employment between 0.5 and 1.0 percent.
